questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Performance Best Practices”?
options: Performance Best Practices helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Performance Best Practices means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Performance Best Practices removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Performance Best Practices should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Performance Best Practices helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Performance Best Practices is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Profile before optimizing” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Profile before optimizing” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Profile before optimizing” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Profile before optimizing” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Profile before optimizing” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Profile before optimizing” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Profile before optimizing” under Performance Best Practices. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Performance Best Practices”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
